paper.title: Online KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation under Misspecification

unmapped: KL-regularized objective: regret measured against the KL-optimal Gibbs policy pi* proportional to pi_ref exp(eta R*), with KL penalty eta^{-1} KL(pi||pi_ref)
General function approximation with a finite reward class R (cardinality N_R) that may be misspecified; pointwise misspecification level zeta_Bandit (sup-norm) assumed known to the learner
Reference policy pi_ref and regularization parameter eta known
Mean reward R* in [0,1], noise conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian
Complexity measured by eluder-style dimension d(R, lambda, T)
settings.definition_quote: At each round t, a context x_t is drawn from an unknown distribution d ... The learner subsequently receives a reward r_t = R^\star(x_t, a_t) + \epsilon_t, where R^\star:\X\times\A\to[0,1] is an unknown ground-truth reward function, and \epsilon_t is conditionally zero-mean and 1-sub-Gaussian. ... Reg(T) = \sum_t (J(\pi^*) - J(\pi_t)), J(\pi) := E_x E_a [R^\star(x,a) - \eta^{-1} KL(\pi(\cdot|x) || \pi_ref(\cdot|x))]

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic MDP reinforcement learning, not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Episodic MDP with horizon H and T episodes, KL-regularized value against stagewise reference policies
Finite stagewise function classes R_h with stagewise pointwise KL-Bellman misspecification zeta_RL (known)
Finite continuation-value classes V_{h+1} for concentration
settings.definition_quote: An episodic MDP is defined by a tuple (S, A, H, T, P, d, r) ... J(\pi) = E_{s_1 \sim d}[V_1^\pi(s_1)], Reg(T) = \sum_t (J(\pi^*) - J(\pi_t)).

symbols.eta_kl: KL-regularization parameter eta (objective penalty eta^{-1} KL)
symbols.N_R: cardinality of the finite reward function class R
symbols.zeta_B: pointwise (sup-norm) misspecification level zeta_Bandit of class R

conditions: regret is KL-regularized regret against the Gibbs-optimal policy
tuning: lambda >~ d(R,lambda,T) + log(N_R T/delta) + T zeta_Bandit^2

source.label: thm:bandit_main
source.quote: Assume the bandit model with conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian noise. Assume the function class is finite with N_R:=|R|<\infty. ... Run Algorithm with the bonus calibrated to the known misspecification level, and choose \beta = \Theta(\sqrt{\log(N_R T/\delta)}). Choose \lambda large enough ... Then, with probability at least 1-\delta, Reg(T) = O(\eta[\log(N_R T/\delta) d(R,\lambda,T) + T\zeta_{Bandit}^2]).

results.notes: Comparator is the KL-optimal Gibbs policy; mapped to best_policy. Recovers Zhao et al. realizable bound when zeta=0.

symbols.d_RL: aggregated RL eluder complexity sum_h d(R_h, lambda, T)

conditions: any optimistic KL-regularized fitted-Q procedure satisfying, w.p. >= 1-delta, confidence/optimism, uncertainty summability, and predictable-to-realized alignment conditions

source.label: thm:rl_modular
source.quote: Consider any optimistic KL-regularized fitted-Q procedure ... Assume that with probability at least 1-\delta, the following conditions hold simultaneously. ... Then, on the same event, Reg(T) = \widetilde O(\eta H^2\beta^2 d_{RL}(\lambda,T) + \eta H^3 T\zeta_{RL}^2).

results.notes: Modular, conditional theorem not tied to a specific algorithm. RL setting is out of scope for bandits.

symbols.d_RL: aggregated RL eluder complexity sum_h d(R_h, lambda, T)

conditions: finite stagewise classes R_h and finite continuation-value classes V_{h+1}
stagewise pointwise misspecification Assumption 3.4 with level zeta_RL
tuning: beta = Theta(sqrt(Lambda_RL)), Lambda_RL = max_h log(4TH N_{R_h} N_{V_{h+1}}/delta)
lambda >~ H^2 + sigma_bar^2 (d_RL + Lambda_RL) + T zeta_RL^2, sigma_bar^2 = Theta(1+H^2)

source.label: thm:rl_main
source.quote: Assume the episodic KL-regularized RL setting ... with conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian reward noise, and assume the stagewise pointwise misspecification condition with level \zeta_{RL}. Assume each stagewise function class is finite ... Run Algorithm with the bonus calibrated to \zeta_{RL}. ... Then, with probability at least 1-\delta, Reg(T) = \widetilde O(\eta H^2 d_{RL}(\lambda,T) + \eta H^3 T\zeta_{RL}^2).

results.notes: beta^2 (log factor) absorbed in O_tilde. Out-of-scope RL setting.
